details: The test imports actual canonical modules and asserts native_qualifier.process_reconciliation is the same module object as the assembled process_reconciliation.
It constructs refs to the actual pinned module, C source, header, dylib, and build receipt; native_provider_query validates those artifacts before returning the callback.

The callback calls the actual run_query_child with boundary_deadline, clock, and the four explicit native module/library path and SHA-256 keyword arguments. The real function signature accepts these kwargs; a non-finite NaN deadline returns invalid-boundary-deadline/not-started with no child PID before process creation.

The wrapper source independently confirms the four forwarded values are the validated absolute paths and exact hashes; the earlier fresh qualifier review records the source-closure and build-receipt checks.
The test builds raw ps-v2 bytes with ucomm 'Cräsh pad' and args containing 'naïve', using bytes.ljust(64) for the fixed ucomm column.

It confirms the parser preserves raw table bytes, yields exactly 64 encoded ucomm bytes, preserves the actual arguments in the classifier projection, matches the native ucomm bytes plus padding, and binds the raw stdout SHA-256. This closes the earlier review's missing multibyte positive-fixture note.
The corrected test patches process_reconciliation.run_query_child.__kwdefaults__['popen'] with a forbidden mock and asserts it was not called.
This replaces the keyword-only default captured when run_query_child was defined, so the no-spawn assertion is effective. The current NaN-deadline path returns before the patched callable.
